content: Anak-anak bilang film baru itu keren
dan sangat menarik dari awal sampai
akhir.
= The kids say the new movie is cool and
gripping from start to finish.
keren is not a word the written cards
would give you. Like bilang, which you
met in Tier 1, it is what people in
Jakarta actually say, and this tier
opens with it on purpose.
From here the pack lets the spoken city in.
Understand every word of it. Write none of
it, until somebody writes it to you first.
Two more cards in this tier do the same:
omong and gampang.
The particles carry no meaning you can look
up. They carry tone, and a sentence without
them sounds cold.
sih   softens, or presses gently   Press 1
dong  come on, please, obviously   Press 2
deh   fine then, all right         Press 3
kok   why on earth, but surely     Press 4
nih, tuh   this here, that there
lho        wait, did you not know
kan        you know it too, right
nah        so, there we are
yah        oh well
They sit at the end of the clause, one at a
time, and never in a letter.
The other half of the city voice is words
cut short.
nggak, gak   tidak                 Press 1
udah         sudah                 Press 2
aja          saja                  Press 3
gimana       bagaimana             Press 4
banget       sangat                Press 5
gue, gua   saya
lu, lo     kamu
gue and lu are Jakarta and young. To an
official, a shopkeeper or anyone older, say
saya, and Pak or Bu for the other person.
Read all of it. Write none of it.
Keadaan rumah tua itu sangat menyedihkan
setelah banjir besar bulan lalu.
= The state of that old house was very
sad after last month's big flood.
menyedihkan looks like a verb. It is an
adjective, and it is built from sedih, sad.
meN- ... -kan on a feeling root does not
mean to do the feeling. It means to cause
it in whoever is watching.
sedih   ->  menyedihkan   saddening
takut   ->  menakutkan    frightening
malu    ->  memalukan     shaming
kagum   ->  mengagumkan   admirable
The person feels it. The thing causes it.
Nine of them run through this tier and the
next, and they behave like adjectives all
the way: sangat menakutkan, very
frightening.
Suara angin malam itu menakutkan.  Press 1
= The sound of the wind that night was
frightening.
Kerja petani tua itu mengagumkan.  Press 2
= That old farmer's work is admirable.
Two of them you already met in Core:
menarik, which pulls you in, and
menyenangkan, which pleases you. Same
machine, same three pieces.

pronunciation_mappings.1: Suara angin malam itu menakutkan bagi anak-anak.

content: Dalam dongeng lama itu, seorang pangeran
dikutuk menjadi burung kecil selama
tujuh tahun penuh.
= In that old tale a prince is cursed
into a small bird for seven whole
years.
Nobody writing English would put it that
way. An English storyteller says a witch
cursed the prince. Indonesian does not, and
the reason is not style.
In Indonesian the thing the sentence is
about comes first. If the story is about
the prince, the prince opens the sentence,
and the verb turns passive to let him.
So di- is the ordinary voice of narrative,
of officialdom and of the news. Half of
what you read will be in it.
Penjahat dalam film itu akhirnya
ditangkap oleh polisi kota.
= The villain in that movie is finally
caught by the city police.
Bunga itu ditanam ibu tahun lalu.  Press 1
= Mother planted those flowers last year.
The second has no oleh, and the doer sits
bare behind the verb.
With aku or kamu the verb takes ku- or
kau-: kubawa, I carried it. With saya the
pronoun stands bare: buku itu saya bawa.

pronunciation_mappings.1: Bunga itu ditanam ibu di depan rumah tahun lalu.
